title: Farage and the £130m even his detractors have missed
gist: Alan Rusbridger argues that on top of about £77m in crypto-billionaire donations to Farage and Reform UK from Ben Delo and Christopher Harborne, GB News backers Paul Marshall and Legatum have absorbed £131.5m of losses running what is effectively a pro-Reform channel, bringing the subsidy from four men above £200m, while Ofcom and the main parties stay passive and Reform plans its own YouTube TV channel.

insights.claim: Crypto tycoon Christopher Harborne gave Nigel Farage £5m about five months ago without Farage declaring it, and has now pledged to match convicted, Trump-pardoned crypto billionaire Ben Delo's £36m for Reform UK.
insights.speaker: Alan Rusbridger
insights.so_what: Crypto wealth is becoming a major funder of UK populist politics; expect regulatory backlash on political donations and possibly crypto.
insights.locator: Just over 20 weeks ago we were shocked

insights.claim: In about five months two men have directed roughly £77m to Farage or to Reform UK Party Limited, a company incorporated in February 2025, amid a row over £72m of Reform crypto donations.
insights.speaker: Alan Rusbridger
insights.so_what: Reform's war chest far exceeds typical UK party funding; raises its odds at the next general election, a key UK political-risk variable.
insights.quote: an astonishing £77m has been tipped the way of Farage himself, or to Reform UK Party Limited
insights.locator: Just as we were absorbing the implications

insights.claim: Labour is making a belated scramble to retrospectively cap party donations after doing little following the Rycroft Review into foreign financial influence in UK politics, published in March.
insights.speaker: Alan Rusbridger
insights.so_what: Watch UK legislation capping donations; its retrospective reach determines how much of Reform's funding survives.
insights.locator: The Starmer government commissioned the Rycroft Review

insights.claim: GB News backers Paul Marshall and the Dubai-based Legatum Group, headed by Christopher Chandler, have absorbed £131.5m of losses since the channel launched five years ago.
insights.speaker: Alan Rusbridger
insights.so_what: GB News is a loss-making, politically motivated asset; its economics depend on owners' willingness to subsidise, not commercial returns.
insights.quote: have absorbed £131.5m of losses since GB News was launched five years ago
insights.locator: Marshall and Legatum, headed by Christopher Chandler

insights.claim: If GB News is treated as the media wing of Farage's project, the total subsidy flowing to him from four men — Delo, Harborne, Marshall and Chandler — tops £200m.
insights.speaker: Alan Rusbridger
insights.so_what: Reframes the scale of concentrated private backing behind a potential governing party.
insights.quote: the total subsidy funnelled his way by just four men tops £200m
insights.locator: Marshall and Legatum, headed by Christopher Chandler

insights.claim: GB News founder Andrew Neil says the channel's investors were 'rabid Brexiteers' who turned it into the Reform channel, just as Fox became Donald Trump's channel.
insights.speaker: Alan Rusbridger
insights.so_what: Insider confirmation of GB News's political alignment strengthens the case for regulatory scrutiny.
insights.quote: Just as Fox basically became the channel of Donald Trump, it’s clear they have turned GB News into the Reform channel
insights.locator: Neil had the idea of creating

insights.claim: GB News has paid Farage more than £600,000 since he became an MP, at a fee of £3,000, and his own company holds nearly half a million GB News shares, possibly about a 2 per cent holding.
insights.speaker: Alan Rusbridger
insights.so_what: Direct financial ties between a party leader and a broadcaster; a conflict-of-interest and impartiality issue.

insights.claim: Ofcom has been effectively asleep on GB News impartiality, allowing Farage to present a show discussing his own donation controversy with only token challenge from guests.
insights.speaker: Alan Rusbridger
insights.so_what: Low regulatory-enforcement risk for partisan UK broadcasters under current leadership.
insights.locator: The pedantic will complain that GB News

insights.claim: Labour appointed businessman Ian Cheshire to succeed Lord Grade as Ofcom chair, which a source described as 'no Thomas Dewey', implying no appetite to take on vested interests.
insights.speaker: Alan Rusbridger

insights.claim: Rusbridger contrasts the complacency over the Reform money with the outrage when the Telegraph might have gone to a UAE-backed US private-equity bid, which Rishi Sunak's government killed with urgent legislation, blocking the Red Bird bid.
insights.speaker: Alan Rusbridger
insights.so_what: Shows UK policymakers can act fast against foreign media money; the asymmetry is political, not legal.
insights.locator: Compare and contrast the howls of outrage

insights.claim: Reform has briefed that it will spend part of its £72m windfall on launching a Reform TV channel on YouTube, with former GB News head of digital Geoff Marsh contracted for 100 days to design it and an initial target of 25 staff, many poached from GB News.
insights.speaker: Alan Rusbridger
insights.so_what: A party-owned channel on YouTube sidesteps Ofcom and may draw talent and audience from GB News; watch GB News economics.
insights.quote: The initial target, I hear, is 25 new staff, many poached from GB News.
insights.locator: The second channel will reportedly broadcast

insights.claim: The existing pro-Reform GB News YouTube channel already has 2.18m subscribers, which the new Reform channel would compete with for attention.
insights.speaker: Alan Rusbridger
insights.so_what: Benchmark for the reach of partisan UK video media outside Ofcom's broadcast regime.
insights.locator: The second channel will reportedly broadcast
